name: csv-export
title: Export invoices as CSV
body:
## Motivation

Finance reconciles invoices in a spreadsheet at month end and today copies them out of `GET /invoices` page by page (FIN-88). They asked for a CSV they can download, and the finance dashboard wants to pull the same file on a schedule.

## Changes

- `GET /invoices/export.csv` returns one row per invoice: number, customerId, status, currency, issuedAt, dueAt, totalCents, lineCount. It takes the same `customerId` and `status` filters as the list, without paging.
- `listForExport` on the repository and the service loads the matching invoices with their lines; totals still come from `computeTotals`, like every other read.
- New `src/lib/csv.ts` with pure `formatRow` / `toCsvRows` helpers, so the formatting is tested without going through HTTP.
- The route streams the rows straight to the response through `reply.raw`, so a big export is not buffered by Fastify's serializer. It is registered in `app.ts` next to `/health`, so the dashboard's scheduled job can pick it up.
- README: a row in the API table and a short section on the export format.

## Testing

- Unit tests for `toCsvRows`: header plus one row per invoice, and the empty case.
- An `app.inject` test that exports with a customer and status filter and checks the exact CSV.
- Ran `pnpm dev`, downloaded an export with curl and opened it in a spreadsheet; columns line up.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are green.

## Open questions

- I kept it simple with a string join, happy to stream if we think exports get big.
